key_insight: Latent-flow world models can look stable during training but still fail at the core task of motion: the manipulated object does not move as intended. The paper shows this is mainly a supervision problem, and that adding decode-based rollout signals can restore meaningful motion without sacrificing stability.
problem_solved: It addresses the silent failure of frozen latent-flow world models that lose motion fidelity in manipulation tasks, where latent-only training either keeps objects still or produces unrealistic teleport-like movement.
method: Diagnose the failure mode by showing that anchor-sparse, latent-only supervision does not specify where motion should occur along the prediction horizon.
Compare latent-only retraining with decode-augmented rollouts to identify why motion quality degrades.
Restore motion by strengthening the training signal with decoder-aware supervision that ties latent predictions to visible object movement.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work clarifies that good latent representations alone are not enough—training signals must explicitly preserve motion. It offers a practical path to build world models that remain cheap and stable while being useful for manipulation.

paper_title: Frozen Flows Forget: Diagnosing and Restoring Lost Motion in a Latent-flow World Model
paper_authors: Xiwen Chen, Rigaudiere Z. Li, Zhiruo Zhou, Xiaojun Zhu, Houde Liu
